I have been working this same land for 25 years and know what it takes in this county. My 20 mu runs wheat and maize on the same plots — winter wheat, then summer maize, same fields. That is how it has always been done here, and it works.

**Wheat (this coming autumn through next June):**
My neighbors and I all plant the county-recommended improved wheat variety — I have used it for years and it gives me steady yields. I will plough before planting to turn over the maize stubble, then apply base fertilizer at sowing. I will top-dress at jointing in spring. Quzhou winters are dry, so I always do the pre-sowing irrigation, the wintering water, one at jointing, and one around heading — four total. I spray herbicide after emergence in winter, then fungicide and insecticide before heading when the rust and aphids come. My yield is usually around 450 kg per mu on good years.

**Maize (next summer):**
Right after wheat harvest in June I do rotary tillage — quick, easy, gets the soil ready fast before I plant maize. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, which I buy every year. I apply fertilizer at planting and again when the plant is knee-high. Summer rains help, but if it goes dry at tasseling I pump from the well twice. Two pesticide rounds — one for stem borer, one if there is fall armyworm pressure. I expect around 600 kg per mu.

With family members earning off-farm income, I do not need to take big risks. I stick to what I know gives reliable returns.
